mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4.5% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% in the month before the prediction window
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during post-tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the 4.5% threshold within the defined window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payrolls surprise exceeding +100,000 jobs (PAYEMS) coinciding with a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% in the prior month predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return via stronger labor market confidence and corporate earnings momentum.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 100,000 AND UNRATE < 4.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: No significant excess returns in 60-day windows where both triggers are met (p > 0.05 in two-tailed test), or UNRATE remains above 4.5% in subsequent months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) of at least 5% year-over-year for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals resilient consumer demand and upward earnings revisions.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly YoY growth ≥ 5% for two consecutive months before prediction
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when the two-month HOUST growth pattern is present (out-of-sample), or the pattern is not statistically significant (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 10% in the prior month, followed by a rebound of at least 5% in the current month, predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it reflects temporary supply-side stress and short-term uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -10% in month t-1 AND INDPRO ≥ +5% in month t
failure_condition: No significant negative 20-day returns during such reversals (p > 0.05), or the pattern is not reproducible in multiple sectors.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three consecutive months indicates disinflation, which is associated with a positive S&P 60-day forward return as markets anticipate a less restrictive policy path.
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day returns during such disinflation windows (p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL re-enters > 3% before the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% followed by two consecutive months of unemployment below 5% predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it signals a cooling labor market and reduced earnings growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5.0% in month t-1 AND UNRATE < 5.0% in months t and t+1
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative during such labor market transitions (p > 0.05), or the pattern is not consistently observed across multiple cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in retail sales (PAYEMS) and manufacturing activity (RSAFS) by at least 2% each, when GDP deflator (CPIAUCSL) is flat for two months, predicts a positive S&P 60-day forward return via dual demand channels and inflation stability.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS ≥ +2% AND RSAFS ≥ +2% AND CPIAUCSL < +0.5% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Dual demand growth with stable inflation
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day returns during such combined signals (p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL rises above 0.5% during the window.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of falling industrial production (INDPRO) for four consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it reflects structural supply constraints and downward earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < baseline (trend) for four consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative during such prolonged contractions (p > 0.05), or the trend reverses before the 20-day horizon.
